text:
Google citations work like references on a job application.

Google checks your name, address and phone number on directories across the web.

All the same? Moving on.
Three different phone numbers? Now Google's wondering which one is you.

Clean up the old ones first.

Order of jobs for a plumber in Bunbury with an ordinary website:

1. Google Business Profile. Free. Right number, right hours, real photos.
2. Reviews from happy customers.
3. The website.

Most people do it backwards. Then wonder why the phone's quiet.

Tiler in Logan runs Google Ads. I ask how many clicks became phone calls.

"No idea. Google handles that."

Google has no idea either. No conversion tracking.

So Google's guessing which clicks worked.
A guessing machine with his credit card.

Locksmith in Parramatta rebrands. "Dave's Keys" becomes "Westside Locksmiths".

New van. New sign.

True Local still says Dave's Keys. So does Yellow Pages. So does a Facebook page from 2017.

Google reads all of it.

Update the old listings the same week you change the sign.

Google's AI Overview describes my "Perth's hardest working SEO expert" page differently on every refresh.

"A clever SEO experiment."
"A playful marketing hook."

Every version names my business and links to my page.

Ask AI Mode about what you do. Are you in the answer?

Every November someone tells me:

"We'll start the marketing in January. Fresh year."

Their customers didn't get the memo. They're searching right now. Booking whoever shows up.

The majority is ALWAYS wrong.

Start this week.
